title: Coarse information and finite rank obstructions for flat lattice Hodge forms
abstract: We study how finite observations and finite-rank repairs can restore coercivity for unit-spacing flat lattice Hodge forms. An explicitly constructed real Fourier band gives necessary output-dimension budgets, including tangent obstructions for differentiable nonlinear observations. Singular Schur compatibility explains why kernel nonnegativity alone is insufficient. Positive results include scalar and matrix critical inverse-moment bounds for global spectral observations, exact finite prescribed-mean penalty thresholds, and constructive spatial means. For coefficients depending on any k < D coordinate directions, we construct actual disjoint rectangular averages with penalty coefficient K = c and the critical target-order observation budget. The construction derives local energy control from the coefficients and charges a balanced base tree through its invariant directions; it handles odd sizes and singleton cells. At least one exactly invariant coordinate remains required by this argument. An explicit corollary of the existing threshold construction handles arbitrary arrangements of scalar coefficient values 1 and H: the actual critical moment gives target-order rectangular means with the same global penalty coefficient K=c. Complementary examples distinguish successful observations from minimum-coefficient, full-tree, point-support and strong Green-moment certificates. The latter have matching all-rectangle certificate-cost regimes. A weaker detour exclusion and an explicit coexact parity example delimit an additional local comparison route. Further exact boundary-energy calculations rule out uniformly controlled exact trace extension based only on internal energy, including near-one critical moments, and, in D ≥ 4, a size-independent sum of separately minimized harmonic costs over disjoint rectangles. The discrepancy also occupies a growing-dimensional space, ruling out uniformly bounded-rank repairs of that particular comparison. The underlying binary family nevertheless admits the constructive partition. Local shell estimates lower the inverse-moment exponent from D/2 to (D-1)/2 with a necessary thickness cost; the thickness-uniform D/2 estimate and sharp local counterexamples are grouped with them. Complete analytical proofs and separately pinned formal endpoints and finite diagnostic records are distinguished throughout. Classical methods are attributed, and originality remains subject to further comparison. The unrestricted critical rectangular problem is open. No interacting or continuum Yang–Mills mass gap is asserted.
